title: Feedback That Changes Behaviour

audience.who: corporate employees who give feedback to peers or reports
audience.knows: feedback matters, but has mostly given it as general praise or criticism
audience.cares_about: getting the other person to actually do something different, without damaging the relationship

outcome: After watching, the viewer can turn a vague comment into feedback that names a specific observed action, its effect, and a clear next step, and can check their own draft before saying it.
through_line: Feedback lands as a feeling unless it points at something the person can see and do differently, so make it about the action, not the person.

arc_plan.what: A colleague gives a well-meant comment after a weak presentation, the receiver nods warmly, and next week nothing has changed. The viewer recognises the scene.
Promise a simple way to rebuild that same comment so the receiver knows exactly what to repeat or change, in under two minutes.
Show why the first comment felt nice but left the receiver with nothing to act on: it described the person, not an action.
Rework the same comment step by step on one board: name the observed action, add its effect on others, then add a clear next step. Each part is named after it is seen.
Give the viewer two or three versions of the comment and have them spot which one the receiver could act on, then reveal why.
Invite the viewer to pick one comment they owe someone this week and rewrite it with the same three parts.
Return to the opening presentation: the reworked comment is delivered, and next week the receiver visibly does it differently.

must_cover.what: Vague or personal feedback leaves good feelings but no change
Describe a specific observed action rather than a trait or judgement
State the effect of that action on others or on the work
Agree a clear, doable next step the person can take
A check where the viewer picks the most actionable feedback

must_avoid: Statistics or research claims without a source
Opening with a formal explanation of terms or an agenda
Lecturing tone; speak as a capable colleague
Examples that appear once and never return
example_posture: One running example, a presentation comment, used for hook, build, check and payoff. Keep it ordinary and workplace-credible, with no invented real people or figures.
visual_direction: Cartoon story with two colleagues in one recurring office situation. A comment that visibly gets rebuilt piece by piece on one board, a before and after of the receiver's behaviour, and one loud thing on screen at a time.
voice_note: Mentor: warm, direct and unhurried, like a senior colleague sharing something that worked. Never talks down.
open_questions: Which named feedback model, if any, should the knowledge sheet anchor to?
Should the example be a presentation or another workplace situation?

inferred: Running example of a presentation comment
